The Criminal Justice, Mental Health, and Substance Abuse (CJMHSA) Reinvestment Grant Program was created by section 394.656, Florida Statutes (F.S.), and is housed within the Department of Children and Families (Department). The purpose of this Request for Applications (RFA) is to provide funding under the Reinvestment Grant Program to counties which they may use to plan initiatives that increase public safety, avert increased spending on criminal and juvenile justice systems, and improve the accessibility and effectiveness of treatment services for adults and juveniles who have a mental illness, substance use disorder, or Co-Occurring mental health and substance use disorders, and who are in, or at-risk of entering, the criminal or juvenile justice systems. NOTICE OF INVITATION TO BID

STATE OF FLORIDA

DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION

BID NO. BDC04-26/27

 

The Department of Environmental Protection, Bureau of Design and Construction is soliciting formal, competitive, sealed bids from Contractors licensed to work in the jurisdiction for the project listed below.

 

PROJECT NAME: Suwannee River State Park – Bathhouse Replacement 

 

BID SUBMITTAL DUE DATE:  No later than 3:30 pm (ET), Tuesday, October 20th, 2026, to the below address: Florida Department of Environmental Protection, Bureau of Design and Construction, 3800 Commonwealth Boulevard, MS #520, Tallahassee, Florida, 32399-3000, Attention: Logan Lee-Marple, Bureau of Design and Construction, (850) 245-2519.  (For hand delivery: Carr Building, Welcome Desk.)  The Department reserves the right to reject any or all bids.

 

BID POSTING DATE: No later than 3:30 pm (ET), Tuesday, October 27th, 2026, unless extended by the Department for good cause.

 

INSTRUCTIONS: Documents for this bid will be available for download on Wednesday, September 16th, 2026. Any firm desiring a Project Manual with the plans for this project may obtain directions by emailing BDC_Contracts@dep.state.fl.us.

  

SCOPE OF WORK: 

Base Bid: 

The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, supervision and permitting, as per the contract documents, for the Bathhouse Replacement and corresponding site improvements project at Suwannee River State Park. 

 

Builder’s Risk is required for this project and must be included in bid price. 

 

Note: Bidder Prequalification is required for all bids.  Each bidder shall provide a copy of its biennial pre-qualification letter from FDEP’s Bureau of Design and Construction.  To request a pre-qualification letter, the bidder should email BDC_Contracts@dep.state.fl.us.  If not pre-qualified, the bidder must submit a current State Contractor license certification or registration and current Corporate Charter registration with the bid. 

Pursuant to Executive Order 07-126 and Section 255.252(3), F.S. the Department requires the proposed project be designed and constructed in accordance with green building standards where applicable.

 

PROJECT MANAGER: Johnathan Williamson, Florida Department of Environmental Protection, Bureau of Design and Construction, 3800 Commonwealth Boulevard, Tallahassee, Florida, 32399.  Telephone Number: (850) 245-2671, Email: johnathan.williamson@floridadep.gov. 

 

PARK LOCATION: Suwannee River State Park, 3631 201st Path, Live Oak, FL 32060.  Park Manager: Erica Lewis, Telephone Number: (386) 365-2501, Email: erica.lewis@floridadep.gov.

 

MINORITY BUSINESS REQUIREMENT: The Department of Environmental Protection supports diversity in its Procurement Program and requests that all sub-contracting opportunities afforded by this bid embrace diversity enthusiastically.  The award of sub-contracts should reflect the full diversity of the citizens of the State of Florida. 

 

ADA REQUIREMENTS: Any person with a qualified disability shall not be denied equal access and effective communication regarding any bid/proposal documents or the attendance at any related meeting or bid/proposal opening.  If accommodations are needed because of disability, please contact Logan Lee-Marple with the Bureau of Design and Construction at (850) 245-2519 at least five (5) workdays prior to openings. If you are hearing or speech impaired, please contact the Florida Relay Services by calling (800) 955-8771 (TDD) or (800) 955-8770 (Voice).

 

E-VERIFY: Vendor/Contractor shall utilize the U.S. Department of Homeland Security’s E-Verify system to confirm the employment eligibility of all persons employed by the Vendor/Contractor during the term of the Contract to perform employment duties within Florida and all persons, including subcontractors, assigned by the Vendor/Contractor to perform work pursuant to the contract with the Department.

 

NOTICE OF RIGHTS:  Notice of Intent to Protest the Bid Specifications must be filed with (received by) the Agency Clerk, Lea Crandall, Department of Environmental Protection, Office of General Counsel, 3900 Commonwealth Boulevard, MS #35, Tallahassee, Florida, 32399-3000, (850) 245-2242, FAX (850) 245-2303, Lea.Crandall@dep.state.fl.us, during the 72-hour period after Bid Specifications are posted on the Vendor Bid System.  Failure to file a Notice of Intent to Protest or a formal, written Protest in accordance with Rule 28-110, F.A.C., within ten days after the 72-hour period ends, as pre­scribed in Section 120.57(3), Florida Statutes, shall constitute a waiver of your right to an administrative hearing on the Bid Specifications under Chapter 120, Florida Statutes.  Rules for bid protests can be found in sections 120.569 and 120.57, F.S., and Chapter 28-110, Florida Administrative Code.  A bid protester shall comply with these statutes and rules.

PROPOSALS ARE REQUESTED FROM QUALIFIED, LICENSED GENERAL CONTRACTORS BY THE STATE OF FLORIDA, DEPARTMENT OF MILITARY AFFAIRS HEREINAFTER REFERRED TO AS OWNER, FOR CONSTRUCTION OF:

PROJECT NUMBER: 224005

FOR: The Florida Army National Guard, Construction & Facility Management Office

General Project Description (See Bid Documents for complete details): This is a full facility sustainment project that will address maintenance, repairs, and lifecycle replacement for buildings, building equipment and systems, utilities, and components of the 16,493 square foot Readiness Center and supporting assets to keep them in good working order.

The intent is to sustain the overall asset inventory and maintain the asset inventory in good working order. The project will include sustainment maintenance and repair of items that at nearing or at the end of their useful life, failing or failed, including complete replacement of items as necessary, which is a function of the Sustainment Work Classification.

Work may include, but is not limited to, the following:

  • Roof repairs/roof replacements for buildings and structures.
  • General maintenance/repair activities to exterior of buildings and structures to keep them in good working order (e.g. seal building envelope(s) from the elements).
  • General maintenance/repair activities in the Readiness Center and support building(s) functional areas outlined in NG PAM 415-12 (e.g. painting, flooring replacement, replace ceiling tiles as necessary, etc.).
  • Repair/replacement of latrines/showers, fixtures, tile, flooring, lockers, etc.
  • Repair/replacement of electrical systems/components.
  • Repair/replacement of water systems and components (potable/non-potable, sewage, irrigation, fire suppression, etc.).
  • Repair/replacement of HVAC systems/components.
  • Repair/replacement of fire alarm system/components (alarm, mass notification system, fire suppression system, etc.).
  • Repair/replace communications system/components as necessary.
  • Repair/replace windows as necessary in order to maintain a secure and efficient facility.
  • Repair/replace fencing/gates as necessary in order to maintain a secure facility.
  • Repair/replace interior and exterior lighting as necessary.
  • Parking Areas (MOV & POV) sealing/re-coating with asphalt (or similar) and re-striping parking spaces.
  • Repair/replace Anti-Terrorism-Force Protection (ATFP) measures as necessary.
  • Drainage/grading work to address any site drainage/stormwater requirements as necessary.
  • Repair/replace signage as necessary.
  • Other sustainment work that is found to be necessary to keep the facility in good working order.

Detail.description:
SALE ADVERTISEMENT

Patterson Loop 26/27 Timber Sale

 

The Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services, Florida Forest Service is seeking sealed bids for the sale of timber. Patterson Loop 26/27 Timber Sale in its entirety spans 254 acres. It is estimated to yield 1,427 tons of pine pulpwood/mulch wood and 165 tons of eucalyptus pulpwood/mulch wood. Broken down by species, this is a per unit sale thinning of approximately 220 acres of planted south Florida slash pine, and a clearcutting of approximately 34 acres of planted eucalyptus in Okaloacoochee Slough State Forest in Hendry County, Florida (see attached maps). These maps, and this project in general, divide the harvest into four separate areas referred to as Areas 1, 2, 3, and 4, corresponding to the stands proceeding West to East. The pine sale areas (Areas 1 and 4) are comprised of 19-23-year-old south Florida slash in the range of 200-400 trees per acre calculated through a range of 5-to-7-inch DBH. Timber available for harvest in Areas 1 and 4 include a 3rd row thinning with selection includes diseased, deformed, defective, forked, and suppressed trees. Both pine sale areas will have a target BA of 30 or higher post-harvest. The two smaller stands totaling 34 acres of planted eucalyptus plantations (Areas 2 and 3) were last clearcut 25 years ago. Areas 2 and 3 will be a clearcut. All areas will require low ground pressure equipment. Sale boundaries are roads, wetlands, fire lines or obvious timber type changes.  This will be an eighteen (18) month contract. Interested parties may obtain complete bid information by contacting James Kavanagh at (239) 690-8031.

The Florida Forest Service reserves the right to reject any and all bids and to waive any irregularity in bids received.

 

Bids will be opened at:

10941 Palm Beach Blvd, Fort Myers, Fl 33905

10/28/2026 10:00 AM, EDT

Detail.title: Longleaf Flatwoods Reserve, Alachua County, River Styx Timber Salvage
Detail.description:
The Governing Board of the St. Johns River Water Management District is requesting sealed quotes for a per ton timber sale comprised of approximately 36.1 acres (“Sale Area”) within the Longleaf Flatwoods Reserve, situated west of County Road 325, in Alachua County, Florida. The Sale Area is in Section 9; Township 11 South; Range 21 East. Sale boundaries include roads and firebreaks. (Maps are included in the attached agreement.)

This timber salvage is due to an Ips beetle infestation. Harvest boundaries are categorized as either Primary or Optional. The Primary area is approximately 36.1 acres in size and designated for clearcut harvest of dead, dying, and green pine. The buyer is not obligated to harvest hardwood trees within this area. Within the Optional area, the buyer may cross the Primary boundary to harvest dead pine only; green pine is not available for harvest. The District’s Project Manager will determine the allowable extent of harvesting within the Optional area. All operations must commence within fourteen (14) calendar days of contract execution. The District estimates the volume of timber conveyed in this Agreement to be 860 tons of pine pulpwood, 126 tons of chip-n-saw, 1,550 tons of saw-timber, but there is no guarantee that the volume is present.

List.title: Customer Service and Records Administration Services for ABLE United

Detail.title: Customer Service and Records Administration Services for ABLE United
Detail.description:
The ABLE United Program requires comprehensive records administration, customer service, reporting, and
operational support services necessary to operate a Qualified ABLE Program. The services summarized below
and detailed further in the example Contract included as Appendix A, represent the minimum required services.
The selected Respondent will provide these services in accordance with the Program disclosures (included as
Appendix B) and the Business Rules (included as Appendix C). Respondents may propose additional
enhancements that provide value to the Program.
3.01(1) Recordkeeping and Account Administration
The selected Respondent will provide full-service recordkeeping and administrative support for ABLE Accounts,
including account establishment and maintenance, processing of contributions and withdrawals, transaction
recordkeeping, tax reporting, and other operational functions necessary to administer ABLE Accounts.
The selected Respondent will also provide debit or prepaid card functionality for ABLE Account Owners as part
of its core service offering.
3.01(2) Customer Service and Participant Support
The selected Respondent will provide participant support services for ABLE Account Owners, contributors, and
prospective participants across multiple contact channels, including telephone, online chat, electronic
communications, and written correspondence. Respondents should be capable of supporting accessible
communications and digital services consistent with ADA requirements.
3.01(3) Technology Platform and Online Access
The selected Respondent will provide a secure, reliable, and scalable technology platform that enables online
account opening and management, contribution and withdrawal processing, investment allocation changes,
and participant access to account information and transaction history. The platform shall be accessible through
web and mobile-compatible interfaces and designed to support a high-quality user experience consistent with
accessibility standards, including compliance with applicable ADA requirements.
The platform shall support integration with third-party systems, including financial institutions, payment processors,
and Program partners, and shall maintain accuracy and consistency across systems. Security controls for the
platform are addressed in Sections 3.01(6), 3.01(10, and 3.01(11).
3.01(4) Governance and Audit Support
The selected Respondent will support Board oversight and Program administration through operational reporting
and reconciliation support. The Respondent must maintain appropriate independent audit reports and provide
documentation supporting operational controls and disaster recovery testing.
3.01(5) Data Ownership and Access
The selected Respondent will maintain Program Data in a secure environment and acknowledges that all
Program Data is owned by the Board. The Respondent shall provide the Board with timely, complete, and
unrestricted access to Program Data for purposes including Program oversight, reporting, audit, and transition to
a successor vendor.
The selected Respondent shall maintain appropriate data access controls, audit logs, and data governance
practices to ensure the integrity, security, and traceability of Program Data. The Respondent shall support data
extraction and delivery in industry-standard, machine-readable formats upon request and shall ensure that
5
Program Data can be transferred to the Board or its designee without delay, degradation, or additional cost
beyond agreed-upon contractual terms.
3.01(6) Data Protection and Security Controls
The selected Respondent will maintain data protection and access controls appropriate for the administration
of financial accounts and compliance with applicable federal and state requirements.
The selected Respondent shall implement controls that include encryption of data at rest and in transit, user
authentication, role-based access controls, and protection of sensitive information.
Requirements for monitoring, fraud and threat detection, and incident response are addressed in Sections 3.01(8)
and 3.01(10).
Requirements for security governance, audits, reporting, and compliance documentation are addressed in
Section 3.01(11).
3.01(7) Investment Option Administration
The selected Respondent will support the administration of Board-approved Investment Options, including the
allocation of contributions and withdrawals and coordination with underlying investment managers and
custodians.
The selected Respondent may also support the administration of an FDIC-insured option if approved by the
Board.
The selected Respondent must perform these services in compliance with applicable federal and state laws,
regulations, and Program requirements governing Qualified ABLE Programs.
3.01(8) Incident Response and Cybersecurity Operations
The selected Respondent will maintain a formal Incident Response Program to support the timely detection,
response, and remediation of system and cybersecurity incidents.
The selected Respondent shall develop and maintain a documented Incident Response Plan that defines roles,
escalation procedures and communication protocols. The Plan shall be reviewed at least annually and updated
as necessary.
The selected Respondent shall notify the Board of any security breach as soon as practicable, participate in
cybersecurity and disaster recovery tabletop exercises led by the Board, and shall coordinate with Board staff
and other service providers during incident response activities.
The selected Respondent shall document and report incidents, including preparing and delivering Root Cause
Analysis (RCA) reports for critical and high-severity events, and shall demonstrate the ability to respond to and
resolve incidents in a manner that minimizes impact to program operations and participants.
3.01(9) Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery
The selected Respondent will maintain Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) capabilities to ensure
continuity of operations in the event of system disruptions or disasters. The Respondent shall develop and maintain
a Business Continuity Plan that addresses operations within the first forty-eight (48) hours of a disruption and shall
conduct annual testing of business continuity and disaster recovery plans. The Respondent shall identify and
remediate any deficiencies.
The selected Respondent shall maintain secure, up-to-date backups of all critical systems and data and shall
demonstrate the ability to sustain and restore operations in a timely manner following system outages,
cybersecurity incidents, or other disruptions.
6
3.01(10) System Monitoring and Threat Detection
The selected Respondent will continuously monitor systems, integrations, and user activity to ensure system
performance, data integrity, and security. The Respondent shall monitor for fraud, suspicious activity,
unauthorized access, and data anomalies. The Respondent shall implement automated alerting and escalation
procedures and shall proactively identify, investigate, and resolve issues to maintain system stability and security.
3.01(11) Security Governance and Compliance
The selected Respondent will maintain a comprehensive security and compliance program and a security
governance framework aligned with applicable regulatory requirements and industry best practices. The
Respondent shall conduct quarterly security audits and user access reviews and shall maintain audit logs for
system access, data changes, and administrative activity.
The selected Respondent shall participate in security training and awareness programs, including phishing
simulations as required by the Board, and shall demonstrate compliance with applicable federal and state
requirements governing financial accounts and data protection. The Respondent shall provide documentation
and reporting to support compliance and audit requirements.
3.01(12) Reporting, Documentation, and Transparency
The selected Respondent will provide operational reporting and maintain documentation necessary to support
Program oversight, audit readiness, and continuity of operations. The Respondent shall provide monthly reporting
on system performance, incidents, and support activity and shall maintain current documentation related to
implementation plans, security plans, business continuity, system configurations, integrations, and security
controls.
The selected Respondent shall provide quarterly reporting on documentation updates, audit findings, and
corrective actions. All documentation shall be maintained in a format that supports audit, compliance, and
transition to a future service provider, if required.
3.01(13) Value-Added Services
The Respondent may offer services other than those specifically outlined in the solicitation that it believes offer
additional operational benefits, efficiencies, or risk reduction (Value-Added Services). Although the Board has
identified its current business needs, those needs are not intended to limit the Respondent’s innovations or
creativity in preparing a Response. The Board will consider innovative ideas, new concepts, and partnership
arrangements not otherwise presented in this ITN, including unique business features, special services, cost savings
or shared-savings arrangements, discounts, or terms and conditions specific to the selected Respondent. If the
Respondent is awarded the Contract and a Value-Added Service is included in the Contract without an
established start date, the Board will provide the agreed-upon notice before the service is implemented.

List.title: Actuarial Services for the Stanley G. Tate Florida Prepaid College Program

Detail.title: Actuarial Services for the Stanley G. Tate Florida Prepaid College Program
Detail.description:
The Prepaid Plan requires independent actuarial analysis supporting the Board’s statutory duty to evaluate the actuarial soundness of the prepaid fund and to establish plan prices (See Appendix D for an overall description of the program). The services below are minimum requirements; the selected Respondent will perform them using data and assumptions supplied or approved by the Board and in accordance with applicable actuarial standards.
3.01(1) Transition Plan
Submit and maintain an orderly transition plan, if applicable. The transition plan should describe the process, details, and schedule for providing an orderly transition from the current provider. The objectives of the transition plan should be to minimize the impacts on continuity of operations, maintain communication with staff, identify key issues, and overcome barriers to transition.
3.01(2) Annual Planning
Meet in person with Board staff at least annually to plan the next 12 months of deliverables. As part of annual planning, review material Program experience, assumptions that may warrant further review, emerging actuarial issues, and potential analytical needs that may support significant Board policy, financial, or Program decisions.
Provide a detailed annual work plan identifying Board data needs, delivery dates, review points, meetings, draft and final deliverables, and dependencies necessary to meet the Board’s schedule.
3.01(3) Data Review
The Board will provide all data necessary to perform the specified contract services. Quarterly, the Actuary shall review, load, reconcile, and evaluate Board-provided data; investigate anomalies; determine whether information is complete and adequate; and recommend data improvements needed for valuations, pricing, and experience studies. (See Appendix I for an example data file).
The selected Respondent shall protect Board data and use appropriate actuarial and statistical systems to perform and document all analyses.
3.01(4) Quarterly Actuarial Valuations and Cash Flows
Prepare four quarterly actuarial valuation letters each year, as of June 30, September 30, December 31, and March 31, using the latest experience data, Board-approved assumptions, and anticipated future years of sales (as directed by the Board). Reports should include information, charts, breakdowns, and explanations in sufficient detail for the Board to understand the actuarial position of the Prepaid Plan.
In addition, monthly undiscounted and discounted cash flows shall be provided to support the appropriate values in the report.
See Appendix F for an example of a quarterly valuation report.
3.01(5) Annual Actuarial Valuation and Cash Flows
Prepare one annual actuarial valuation report as of June 30. The report will update actuarial projections, include requested sensitivity analyses, reconcile surplus, review experience, recommend assumption changes when
4
appropriate, provide the program termination liability as provided for in Section 1009.98(8) Florida Statutes and with Board guidance, and provide projected undiscounted and discounted monthly cash flows.
The Respondent shall review and analyze at least one major actuarial valuation assumption each year.
See Appendix G for an example of an Annual Actuarial Adequacy Report
NOTE: The annual actuarial adequacy review treats the Program as closed for valuation purposes, evaluating existing contracts without assuming any future sales. This approach does not mean the Program is closed to new purchases. Because the Program continues to sell plans each year, the quarterly actuarial reviews include estimated additional years of sales, as directed by the Board, and the associated future receipts and obligations. The resulting quarterly cash flow projections are used to construct the liability-driven investment (LDI) benchmark, aligning the investment strategy with projected net cash flows from both existing contracts and anticipated future sales.
3.01(6) Sensitivities
Develop with the Board and periodically update a sensitivity matrix for material actuarial drivers. Where reasonably practicable, present the results in a form that helps staff understand the directional and approximate effect of defined changes on actuarial adequacy, projected cash flows, and plan pricing, together with appropriate limitations.
3.01(7) Annual Plan Pricing
Prepare one annual Prepaid Plan pricing report each year for the designated enrollment period (currently July 1 through June 30), including plan prices by payment option and beneficiary age for each offered product. Test price adequacy, determine and disclose break-even rates of return, and provide illustrative prices at alternative inflation assumptions upon request.
The Respondent shall review and analyze at least one major pricing assumption each year.
See Appendix H for an example of the Annual Plan Pricing.
3.01(8) Supporting Files
Provide electronic actuarial and pricing reports and usable supporting files, including payoff factors and projected cash flows, sufficient for Program operations, benchmark development, review of Board inputs and assumptions, and understanding of results.
3.01(9) Board Presentations and Consultation
Appear before the Board annually, to explain and substantiate the annual actuarial adequacy and pricing reports.
Consult with Board staff by letter, telephone, electronic communication, or in person upon request.
3.01(10) Professional Standards and Quality Control
Perform all services in accordance with applicable qualification standards, Actuarial Standards of Practice, and the Actuarial Code of Professional Conduct. Maintain documented review and quality-control procedures for all deliverables.
3.01(11) Continuity
Maintain a continuity plan, update it, and provide it to the Board annually, and cross-train personnel to preserve knowledge of the Prepaid Program.
5
3.01(12) Data Security and Confidentiality
Maintain appropriate controls for confidential Board data, limit access to authorized personnel, use secure transmission and storage methods, and promptly report any incident affecting Board information.
3.01(13) Records, Documentation, and Audit Support
Maintain work papers, models, assumptions, data reconciliations, and supporting documentation sufficient to reproduce and explain conclusions and to support Board oversight, audit, and transition to a successor provider.
3.01(14) Coordination and Responsiveness
Coordinate with Board staff and other Board service providers, respond promptly to questions, identify emerging issues, and communicate any matter that may affect the accuracy, quality, or timeliness of deliverables.
3.01(15) Additional Actuarial Reports, Letters, or Assumption Studies
At the Board’s request, conduct additional actuarial adequacy reports or letters, pricing reports or letters, or assumption studies.
3.01(16) Additional Actuarial Advisor Studies and Services
At the Board’s request, and subject to advance written scope and fee approval, conduct additional sensitivity analyses, single-plan pricing analyses, or other special actuarial projects not identified above.
3.01(17) Workshops
At the Board’s request, prepare and present an in-person workshop on calculations, data, assumptions, legislative changes, reporting, or improvements to models and methods.
3.01(18) Representation
At the Board’s request, represent the Board before governing authorities on actuarial matters.
3.01(19) Legislation
At the Board’s request, assist with preparation or review of legislation, fiscal notes, and bill analyses.
3.01(20) Other Value-Added Services
Respondents may propose actuarial tools, dashboards, modeling enhancements, training, benchmarking, process improvements, or other services that provide additional value, efficiency, transparency, or risk reduction to the Board.
Note: Illustrative annual adequacy, quarterly valuation, and pricing reports are informational and do not limit the Board’s ability to modify requirements during negotiations.

The District is seeking the assistance of experienced contractors to provide Large-Capacity commercial and industrial chillers, rated at 2,000 tons or more for installation, repair and emergency response for a three-year continuing contract term. Services will included at least twenty-six (26) chillers at five (5) different locations throughout the District.

Typical items of work may include, but are not limited to chiller repairs, chiller cleaning, chiller removal, chiller motor installation, and industrial HVAC repairs. In addition, this contract shall serve to provide the District with emergency response for minor repairs.

List.title: LIMS Maintenance & Technical Support Services

Detail.title: LIMS Maintenance & Technical Support Services
Detail.description:
Maintenance and support of the Florida Department of Law Enforcement’s (FDLE) Forensic Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) that provides evidence tracking, inventory, and auditing capabilities. This system accommodates multi-discipline services, including but not limited to Biology, Firearms, Chemistry and Toxicology. The current LIMS was acquired through competitive solicitation (RFP B1011) from Porter Lee Corporation in 2007 and is an essential element in maintaining FDLE Regional laboratories forensic accreditation standards. Since initial implementation, FDLE has acquired additional modules for the LIMS system, including the investigation’s Evidence Management System, Radio Frequency Identification System, .Net LIMS System, Toxicology Automation Module, Prelog v2, Android Software for Custody Transfer and Inventory Modules, as well as the Biology Automation Module. 

The purpose of this single source request is to request that FDLE continues to receive system maintenance and support services required for FDLE’s existing Laboratory Information Management System and Evidence Management System, Radio Frequency Identification System, Criminal Evidence Intake Module, .Net LIMS System, Toxicology Automation Module, Prelog v2, Android Software for Custody Transfer and Inventory Modules, and Biology Automation Module.   

This system maintenance is critical to ensure that FDLE continues to meet business needs and national forensic laboratory standards.
